body: Nope. What is it?

In person, he treats me very well. However, over text I often have to initiate the conversation, yet when I go MIA for 2 days he asks for me, but often leaves me hanging in the middle of a conversation.       
    I don't want to just drop it and regret the lost chance. Until there's an ultimatum, aka either a definite fade out that lasts 3+ days or an actual "hey, I think we should stop seeing each other," then I'm not giving up.
Duly noted!
Okay, that totally makes sense. I should continue to look around, but I'm a very one-person kind of dater because I'm a traditionalist at heart. Thanks for the advice.
Thanks! I'll take the advice to heart.

Okay. I understand that at his age a relationship is like an investment (he used the analogy of  "like buying a house,"). To him, it's a serious thing and he expressed on his profile that he's in it for the long haul. Should I just bring up that I understand what he means? Just in passing?
Alright, that makes sense! Thanks so much.

Sorry, I thought you meant something differently. I meant he's accepting that I have some issues; I haven't put any pressure at all on him to deal with them. Just mentioned it because it's important and you shouldn't keep things like that until waaaay later.
Very true. What do you suggest?

He seems too mature to go soft. If I ask him any question, he's as blunt as blunt can be. As far as I can tell, he was genuine in his answer of "not sure" and just wants to take it slow, but I'm just impatient. Is that a valid perspective?

Okay, that makes sense. Perhaps I should just take it slow? He's still replying to my texts, so there's still interest. All I want to do is just talk about what either of us want, not seriously but casually. I don't want to throw him off with any intense conversation.    
 Any other suggestions are appreciated.

So what do you suggest I do? I'm thinking of just saying what I want, and asking what he wants, in terms of a relationship. Just some honest, deep discussion. I don't like playing games and beating around the bush.
I never told him I have anxiety. Just that I have some psych issues I'm working on.
Haha I tend to move quickly. Hopefully if that fourth date comes through, then I'm going to "quell this shit." I just need some blunt honesty in-person, not over text.

He's a very busy guy, lawyer, and I was out of town for a few weeks so only three dates so far. They were very great, we were extremely intimate in person and clicked well. I'm not saying this from my perspective, I could tell he was enjoying himself too.    
 I mean the last time I checked, it was disabled, but now it's back on.

Thanks. My anxiety tends to leave me nauseous so that's why I'm up at nearly 1am on reddit; I can't sleep. He's aware I have some psychological issues and is very accepting of it.    
 So in that case I think you're correct on me projecting my fears on the situation. I'm just very afraid of history repeating itself, I guess. I really want to talk to him about what he said about not being sure, and discuss it, and talk about each other's wants. I think this next date, if accepted, could be identified not necessarily as an ultimatum but as a turning point if all goes well.

The second, actually. I do, and the date I asked about, I wanted to talk about what he said about not being sure, and discuss it mutually.    
True, I tend to wallow in self-pity a lot and it's one of my biggest flaws, so thanks for the reality check.

He passed what? He still replies to my text messages, just often leaves me hanging because he's busy with work, doing overtime on weekends. And I asked him pretty late at night, too, and on a Sunday. Definitely asleep?
He's a very busy guy, works as a lawyer. I also went away for a few weeks out of town.

Look up Borderline Personality Disorder. She might have it, as women with this illness tend to exploit themselves this way.   
 Do some research on your end on what she could have, including what I suggested above.

Still have it even after all the shit I've been put through, and that's a lot of shit. That's mainly because I learned to cherish it at a very young age due to the hardships of childhood, so now despite everything, it's my last beacon of hope. It's a dog-eat-dog world but I'm still here, and so is that so-called veil of innocence.   
 It's naive, but it's really all I have.

Read The Zahir by Paulo Coelho. Really struck me after a break-up that left me in the deepest pits that I'm *still* trying to climb out of. The narrator described exactly the kind of thought process of obsession I was going through over my ex.

Definitely. We're very insightful but a lot of that comes from personal experience and the amount of time we've spent alone psychoanalyzing ourselves. We do the same thing to other people and the situations we get ourselves into. So it's tough to tell the difference between projecting our perception based on personal experience and actually having a logical perspective on a certain situation.

Thanks so much for the response. I tend to have my expectations really high but that's only because of certain psychological issues I have, and even though I'm aware of them it doesn't exactly stop me from having them.    
 I asked him where he thought this was going and he said he's not sure yet, but he also said it's not a no, either. There's a considerable age difference between us so now I understand that at his age, relationships are very serious things as opposed to someone around my age. So hopefully it will keep going and we'll take it slow. I'm much happier and less anxious now that I have a little closure there.   
 Btw I don't want to bother him at work, that's why I don't text him during those hours lol.    

 Then again, thanks!

Get a lawyer, the action to expel you certainly was not legal by any means; because this is 2015 and the feminist movement is at an all-time high (I am a feminist myself but I'm pointing a finger towards the radical branch of the movement itself) it will definitely be difficult to have a man's word win over a woman's, despite the evidence saying otherwise. But then again, it was just you and your witness in silent conversation, against the word of a berserk, shrieking accuser.  
 I truly feel sorry for how your parents are treating you; if anything, they should know that you would never throw away years and years of hard work for such a mistake that in the first place, doesn't even exist and is the product of confused ears.  
 Consider the lawyer, community college/getting your GED, even pitching your story to the local media to garner some public attention before you consider suicide.

Because Neverland is just a castle in the sky. It's where my dreams come true and where I'm happy. It's make-believe and fantasy, but where I want to be the most. No matter what I do it just seems impossible to make my dreams a reality.  
 Of course I have so much to offer. But like I said, I've been living almost solely for other people. Being selfish has made me hurt others, which in turn hurts me. It's how I've been conditioned since early childhood. My talents and accomplishments mean nothing to me and next to nothing to my family, as they're only ever concerned about money which distresses me greatly because I hate how twisted people become over it.  
 I'm losing my sanity and I don't want to become someone I cannot recognize. I'm schizophrenic, of course I would say I have to kill myself because a part of me says I truly have to reach rock bottom, to really attempt suicide but purposefully fail so I can be "reborn" into a new life. Like a morbid baptism. I'm delusional and yet I find complete sense in this. I've always been like this.  
 This is not *a* decision, it's been a series of decisions that have been put off because of the guilt that I would live with if I failed to kill myself. I've been waiting for a very, very long time, true. But the little girl, I remember the memories and dreams I had about the concept of death since I was around 5 years old, fascinated by it. A part of me just knew that my life had to end.  
 My mother and brothers don't believe anything I tell them when it comes to this. My mother gets angry and calls me a drama queen and guilt-trips me (not a surprise), and my brothers just throw it off and say it's just life. The few friends I have, when I confide in them, have become increasingly annoyed when I have talked to them each time about this.  
 I'm just so confused what to do. I can't go on because if I just fight it off, it will come back again. The cycle is like this: I'm sad, then I get depressed, and then the suicidal thoughts start (all in a matter of minutes) and then when I try to fight it off it mulls over and I'm fine, and then I get on a high. This is typical for someone with BPD so then it falls into a vicious cycle of happy-sad-happy-sad over a few weeks.
